answer: A decentralized network resists sybil attacks by requiring every identity to accumulate witnessed work before its voice carries weight. A new account starts at zero, with nothing granted. The protocol treats this unproven state as a faint comet: visible from afar but lacking mass. Each verified contribution adds weight, building a canyon of proven history. Established identities stand on an island of trust, surrounded by evidence. Because voting weight follows witnessed tenure rather than key count, synthetic accounts stay adrift while genuine contributors form a solid island of trust.
